Artificial Intelligence Engineering (Ph.D.)
Location(s): Brookings Main Campus, Online
Program Coordinator/Contact
Rajesh Kavasseri, Interim Department Head
Jun Huang, Assistant Professor and Graduate Coordinator
McComish Department of Electrical Engineering and Computer Science
Daktronics Engineering Hall 214
605-688-4526
Program Information
The Ph.D. in Artificial Intelligence Engineering (AIE) program prepares students to conduct original research at the intersection of AI, computer science, and engineering. The program equips doctoral students with deep analytical, computational, hardware, and ethical foundations needed to design and study intelligent technologies that learn from data and support high-stakes human decision-making. Building on strong preparation in computer science, AI, and hardware systems, students advance and apply these skills in domains where the university has established engineering strengths. Through faculty-led research groups, advanced seminars, interdisciplinary collaborations, and industry- or agency-informed projects, students develop and evaluate data-centric, intelligent systems that tightly integrate hardware and software. Graduates are prepared to lead as research scientists, engineering leaders, and faculty, and to strengthen cross-departmental collaboration by translating AI fundamentals into impactful, research-driven applications across these priority areas.
Available Options for Graduate Degrees
Doctor of Philosophy
72 Credit Plan
Core Requirements
AIE 501 - Artificial Intelligence Engineering Credits: 3
AIE 898D - Dissertation (COM) Credits: 1-9 (30 credits required)
CSC 705 - Design and Analysis of Computer Algorithms (COM) Credits: 3
CSC 770 - Software Engineering Management (COM) Credits: 3
EE 569 - Fundamentals of High-Performance Computing Credits: 3
GE 701 - Research Colloquium 1 Credits: 1
GE 702 - Research Colloquium 2 Credits: 1
GE 703 - Research Colloquium 3 Credits: 1
Electives Credits: 27
Courses Supporting the Ph.D. Program
Up to 30 credits from a completed master’s degree may be applied to a doctoral program at the discretion of the Graduate Student Advisory Committee.
Additional Admission Requirements
GRE: Not Required
TOEFL iBT: 4.5
TOEFL Essentials: 9.5
IELTS: 6.5
Duolingo: 115
Three letters of reference (at least one from a faculty member familiar with the applicant’s research ability; for applicants with a master’s degree, one letter should be from the master’s advisor, if available), a statement of research interest and intent with a focus on the proposed area of research, transcripts, and a resume.
General Requirements
Graduate students must consult with their advisor before registering for graduate coursework. For additional information, refer to the Doctor of Philosophy Degree Requirements.
